title: Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid: A Visitor's Guide to Dahshur
excerpt: Visit the Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid at Dahshur: Sneferu's test runs before Giza. Going inside the Red Pyramid is included in the EGP 200 site ticket.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Yes, you can go inside the Red Pyramid at Dahshur, and entry is included in the Dahshur site ticket with no extra charge. Dahshur, about 35 to 40 km south of Cairo, holds Sneferu's Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid: the failed experiment and the first successful true pyramid, built about 4,600 years ago as the training ground for Giza. Crowds are far thinner than at Giza; allow 1.5 to 2 hours.

UNESCO describes the pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur as one World Heritage site.

You have the Giza pyramids planned: every itinerary says so. What most itineraries skip is Dahshur, the quiet desert site south of Cairo where Egypt first worked out how to build a true pyramid. This guide covers Sneferu's Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid: why one bends, why the other matters more, whether you can go inside (yes, and it is included in the ticket), and how long to allow. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, lists a Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur day trip; its founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid: Sneferu's two test runs

The Bent Pyramid and Red Pyramid are the work of King Sneferu (reigned about 2613 to 2589 BC), founder of the Fourth Dynasty and father of Khufu, the builder of the Great Pyramid. Dahshur is where his engineers learned, by trial and error, what a pyramid could and could not do: the drafting notes for Giza.

Bent Pyramid Red Pyramid
What happened Work started steep, at about 54°, and the upper part flattens to about 43°: the "bend" Built at a steady, safe slope of about 43°; the first successfully completed true (smooth-sided) pyramid
Approximate size About 101 m tall today About 104 m tall; Egypt's third-tallest pyramid after Khufu's and Khafre's
Going inside Interior reopened to visitors in 2019; when open, entry is included Open, included in the site ticket

Sneferu had already worked at Meidum, in the Fayoum, where a pyramid built in stages and finished with smooth sides lost much of its outer structure. Meidum is a separate trip: it is on the Fayoum Oasis, Meidum & Hawara day tour, from €64 per person, as listed in November 2026, and does not include Dahshur. The Red Pyramid's success made Giza possible: Khufu scaled up his father's design a generation later.

Can you go inside the Red Pyramid?

Yes. You can walk inside the Red Pyramid, and it is included in the standard Dahshur site ticket. The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities price list shows Dahshur as a single ticket, and current visitor guides confirm there is no extra charge for the interior, unlike Giza, where the Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure interiors each have their own tickets. A guard at the entrance lets you in.

One ticket rule: the Dahshur site ticket covers the Bent Pyramid, the Red Pyramid and the walk inside the Red Pyramid. At Giza, every pyramid interior is a separate ticket. Dahshur is where you step inside a pyramid without paying again.

The entrance sits high on the north face, reached by a long modern staircase of about 125 steps with a handrail. From there a low passage, roughly 63 m long, slopes down to the first chamber, and you stoop for most of it. The chambers have high corbelled ceilings, meaning the limestone walls step inward layer by layer. It is warm, dusty and genuinely tight, and the chambers are bare. If confined spaces bother you, or if you have back or knee problems, stay outside: the pyramid's scale against the empty desert is the sight.

The Bent Pyramid: why it bent

The Bent Pyramid bends because its builders corrected course mid-build. Work began at about 54 degrees, a steep slope, but the structure showed signs of strain, so the crew flattened the upper part to about 43 degrees. The result is Egypt's most distinctive silhouette, and one of very few pyramids that still wears much of its original smooth casing. Its interior reopened to visitors in July 2019, after decades closed, once a lighting system and walkway were installed. Pyramid interiors at Dahshur can close at short notice for conservation, so treat access as something to confirm on the day.

What else to see at Dahshur, and how long to allow

Allow 1.5 to 2 hours: that covers both pyramids, the ticket gate and the Red Pyramid interior at an easy pace. The site opens from 08:00 to 17:00, and hours shorten in Ramadan, so check before you travel. The Black Pyramid of Amenemhat III, a crumbling Middle Kingdom mudbrick pyramid, also stands in the Dahshur field. There is no shade, no café and little signage, so carry water. Visit between October and April for bearable heat. Dahshur stays calm even in high season, a contrast with the Giza plateau.

Getting to Dahshur from Cairo

Dahshur lies about 35 to 40 km south of central Cairo, roughly an hour by road. There is no practical public transport, and return taxis from the site can be hard to find, so travellers arrive by tour or with a hired car and driver, almost always combined with Memphis and Saqqara in one day. One warning for self-drivers: some satellite-navigation routes via the Fayoum road pass through a military base that is off-limits, so use a driver who knows the Saqqara road. On the Sawa departure, hotel pickup is included and the day runs in this order:

  1. Memphis. The colossus of Ramesses II and the alabaster sphinx.
  2. Saqqara. Djoser's Step Pyramid, Egypt's oldest pyramid. The Serapeum is a separate ticket and is not included.
  3. Lunch between the sites, included.
  4. Dahshur. The Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid, with time to walk around both. Going inside the Red Pyramid is covered by the site ticket; your guide advises on the day.
  5. Back to Cairo. The whole day runs about 9 hours.

The verdict on visiting Dahshur

The Bent and Red pyramids are the missing first chapter of Giza: one failed slope, one first success, in desert quiet, with the Red Pyramid's interior included in the site ticket. faq.q: Is there a separate ticket to enter the Red Pyramid?
faq.a: No. The Dahshur site ticket covers the whole site, including the walk inside the Red Pyramid. The Ministry price list shows Dahshur as a single ticket with no separate interior charge, unlike Giza. The ticket costs EGP 200 for a foreign adult (about €3 at EGP 60 to the euro, 8 November 2026).

faq.q: Can you enter the Bent Pyramid too?
faq.a: When it is open, yes. The Bent Pyramid's interior reopened in July 2019, and when open, entry is included in the standard ticket, but interiors can close at short notice for conservation, so confirm on the day. If you enter only one pyramid, most travellers pick the Red: it is the more straightforward climb.

faq.q: Is going inside the Red Pyramid claustrophobic?
faq.a: Honestly, somewhat. The entry passage is low and roughly 63 metres long, sloping down to the first chamber, and the air inside is still and warm. A handrail and wooden steps make the climb straightforward, but you will be stooping for a minute or two. If tight spaces bother you, skip it: the exterior and the desert silence are the real sight.

faq.q: Is Dahshur worth visiting after seeing the pyramids of Giza?
faq.a: Yes, and arguably it should come first. This is where the design was solved: the Bent Pyramid shows the mistake, the Red Pyramid the fix, and both stand a short drive apart in open desert. Add the chance to enter a pyramid at no extra charge, and Dahshur is the best complement to the Giza plateau.

faq.q: How far is Dahshur from Saqqara?
faq.a: Dahshur lies about 10 km south of Saqqara, a short drive, which is why the two are almost always paired with Memphis in one day loop from Cairo. The standard route runs Memphis first, then Saqqara for the Step Pyramid of Djoser, then Dahshur for the Bent and Red pyramids.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure does not fill?

If a date has not reached four seven days before the tour, it is cancelled, you pay nothing, and Sawa suggests another date. Once confirmed, the date is not cancelled for low numbers, even if one traveller drops out.
